newsitem.title: USA: NYC exceeded overtime budget by 9 pct - comptroller.
newsitem.headline: NYC exceeded overtime budget by 9 pct - comptroller.

text.p: The New York City comptroller on Thursday faulted the Giuliani Administration for spending nine percent more than it had budgeted on overtime during the first half of fiscal 1997.

Mayor Rudolph Giuliani, a Republican, in November revised the budget for overtime to $200.4 million for the first half of the year, attributing the rise in overtime spending in part due to increased police patrols to clean out drug dealers.
But the Administration exceeded this amount by $17.3 million. And in the first two quarters, overtime spending exceeded the year-ago period by $33.6 million, Alan Hevesi said, in prepared remarks.

The total number of city workers at year-end slipped to 234,935, which was 1,322 below the total the Administration forecast. Hevesi, a Democrat, noted that the Department of Social Services has 737 fewer employees than planned.

While the police department has 8,677 more civilian employees than the 6,809 total it is supposed to have, Hevesi explained that this is because the grant from the Federal Crime bill for fiscal 1997 has not yet been received. Those funds will be used pay for 1,900 civilians.
